content:
## Source
.design/m5/47-trust-model.md — full design.

## What this epic delivers
A `polaris-trust` crate exposing a pure `weight(observation, policy, now) -> f32` function. Replaces v1's flat per-upstream weight with per-source × per-category × per-subject-class × time-decay composition. Backwards-compatible with v1 JSONB (a v1 `{"flat": 0.8}` continues to work). Audited policy changes via existing v1 hash-chained audit log.

## Sub-issues (8 PRs + 1 Q-resolution, PR 8 conditional)
- Q-resolution: DSL vs structured (Q1), decay model (Q2), audit UX (Q3), v1→v2 deser (Q4), default policy (Q5), boost-attack mitigations (Q6)
- PR 1: `polaris-trust` skeleton — `TrustPolicy` struct, `weight()` with flat-only, property tests for AC-1/AC-3, replaces v1's lookup (behavior-equivalent)
- PR 2: per-category weight composition; AC-5
- PR 3: time decay (`TimeDecay::half_life_days`); AC-4
- PR 4: per-subject-class weight
- PR 5: templates + admin endpoints (`GET/POST /api/admin/upstream-labelers/<id>/trust-policy`) + audit-log entry for changes (REQ-6 / AC-7)
- PR 6: preview UI in `polaris-frontend` admin surface
- PR 7: `polaris trust-policy explain <obs_id>` command + per-observation weight visibility in case view
- PR 8: conditional — DSL or richer custom expression (gated by Q1 = B or C)

## Provisional answers
- Q1: A (structured config only — covers all stated cases; B as follow-up if operator demand justifies)
- Q2: A (exponential half-life — mathematically clean; operators understand half-life by analogy)
- Q3: C + A (per-observation visibility in case view + admin filter UI)
- Q4: B (versioned discriminator `"version": 2` + one-time data migration on existing rows)
- Q5: A (v1 flat weight unchanged — upgrade must not silently change outcomes)
- Q6: A + B baseline (hard cap at save + hard cap at evaluation); C + D as follow-ups

## Rust-quality notes
- **`polaris-trust` is a pure-logic leaf crate.** No DB deps, no `tokio`, no `reqwest`. Per rust-quality §6: trivially testable.
- **`weight()` is a pure function** taking `(&Observation, &TrustPolicy, DateTime<Utc>)`. Per rust-quality §1: returns `f32` in `[0.0, 1.0]`. Defense-in-depth clamp at end ensures the type invariant holds even with a malformed policy.
- **Multiplicative composition** keeps each factor independent. Order-of-evaluation safety is a property test (`prop_assert_eq!(weight(o, p, t), weight(o, &reordered(p), t))`).
- **`TrustPolicy` serializes to JSONB via serde.** Versioned discriminator pattern (Q4-B): `#[serde(tag = "version")]` enum with v1 and v2 arms. The v2 arm contains the rich struct.
- **Save-time validation** uses `thiserror`'s structured errors (`TrustPolicyError::WeightOutOfRange { field: &'static str, value: f32 }`). The validation function is pure; the save endpoint surfaces it as `400 Bad Request` (REQ-7 / AC-6).
- **`explain()` returns a structured `Decomposition` struct** so both the CLI (`trust-policy explain`) and the case-view UI render the same data. Per rust-quality §9: shared data shape, multiple presenters.
- **Audit-log integration**: changing a policy writes a `kind = 'trust-policy-change'` entry containing serialized old + new policy. The v1 hash chain absorbs this naturally (it accepts any structured payload).
- Per rust-quality §7: property tests via `proptest` cover AC-1 (output range) and AC-3 (v1 backcompat).
